hypotheses.basis: 'Only after' is read as a strict necessary condition: payment must be satisfied before permission to lift exists. Lifting without payment is the sole violation; with payment, permission is granted (though other unstated conditions may also apply).
unresolved_terms: whether other conditions beyond payment may also be required for permission

hypotheses.basis: 'Only after' is read as a biconditional: payment is both necessary and sufficient for permission. The word 'only' restricts the permission gateway exclusively to the payment state, implying no other path to permission exists and payment alone guarantees it.
unresolved_terms: whether 'only after' truly implies sufficiency or merely exclusivity of the condition
whether the second violation clause (not lifting after payment) is a genuine obligation or merely a permissive statement

hypotheses.basis: The policy is read as creating only a positive permission gate, not a prohibition. 'Permitted only after' restricts when permission exists but does not itself declare a violation for acting outside that window. Lifting before payment is unauthorized by this policy, but the policy does not generate a violation clause — it is silent on the pre-payment case, leaving it to other rules or to default status.
unresolved_terms: whether absence of permission constitutes a violation or merely a lack of authorization

hypotheses.basis: 'Only after' is read as a one-time temporal trigger rather than a persistent state condition: once the payment event has occurred, the permission is permanently unlocked regardless of whether the state later reverts (e.g., new overdue bills appear). The condition is on the history of the state, not its current value at the time of lifting. With the available atoms this cannot be fully expressed; the closest encoding treats the permission as unconditional once triggered, which collapses to an unconditional permission clause.
